A write-ahead log (WAL) is a journal that a database keeps of all changes made to its data. This log is used to ensure that the database can recover its data in the event of a power failure or crash, in which the data may be inconsistent and the database may need to be restored to a known good state.

## Step 1: Introduction to Write-Ahead Log
A write-ahead log (WAL) is a critical component of many database systems, designed to ensure data consistency and integrity in the face of system failures. It works by keeping a record of all changes made to the database before they are written to the actual data storage.

## Step 2: Process of Writing to the Log
When a database modification is made, such as an insert, update, or delete operation, the database first writes a record of this change to the write-ahead log. This record contains information about the operation, including what data was modified and how. The log entry is guaranteed to be written before the actual data is modified, hence the name "write-ahead."
